why: One CI guard and its own self-test, plus the run_guards line that invokes it and two backlog rows. scripts/ci/check_document_index.py gains R6 -- a committed DOCUMENT-INDEX row whose status a fresh build_rows() does not reproduce, which R3 structurally cannot see because the header and the row are written by the same --write run and agree with each other. No src/, no config/, no deploy/, no order path, no live-VM mutation, no secret, nothing in LANDING_MACHINERY. R6 IS DIFF-SCOPED AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING, not timidity: 47 rows on main today disagree with a fresh build, so an unscoped rule would fail every PR in the repo from the moment it merged -- an outage, not a guard. The standing number is CENSUSED on every run including a clean one (the session-registry-guard precedent), so the narrow enforcement cannot hide it, and a `scope is None` run produces no findings and says so rather than reading as a pass. Evidence is planted-defect PLUS a real end-to-end demonstration: a scratch edit to a drifted document made the guard exit 1 naming that exact row and the reverted tree exits 0; five mutations each shown to land (pattern count asserted) and each shown to fail --self-test, control quiet. ONE OF THOSE PLANTS FOUND A COLLAPSED STATE IN THE FIX ITSELF -- row_status_drift returned [] for both `nothing drifted` and `could not compute`, so replacing the None guard with an empty dict passed the whole suite; it now returns a NAMED state and the self-test asserts the state, and that is recorded rather than quietly repaired. Full guard set 99 pass / 1 fail, the one being this guard pre-arming, with SKIP 0 because touching run_guards.py runs every guard. The second commit is a register-only observation of U22's carrier running on a real runner; it rides here because it is one updates entry in a file this PR already modifies, and a separate PR would add a seventh branch contending for the most conflict-prone register in the repo.
